alerts.reason: March net sales fell 3.9% year over year as higher prices partly offset fewer pounds sold (A, B). Pricing also supported nine-month sales (D). I expect that support to keep June above -5%, with continued volume losses widening the decline by July–September. Relative to March, it would take only 1.1 percentage points of deterioration to reach -5%.

March net product sales fell 3.3% year over year as volumes declined despite higher realized prices (A, B). Customers and consumers were increasingly resisting those prices (D). I expect pricing to keep the June sales decline under 5%, then offset less of the volume loss in July–September, taking the decline to at least 5%.

March revenue rose just $9 million on $6.4 billion as a roughly $300 million IET gain offset a roughly $300 million OFSE decline spanning North America and international markets (A–C). I expect IET growth to keep June above -5%. Management's outlook for downward oil-price pressure (D) points to further OFSE weakness that could overwhelm the offset in July–September.

March net sales rose 6.5%, but the order backlog fell $157.2 million year over year to $402.6 million, a 28.1% decline (A–C). Remaining orders could sustain June shipments above the threshold. The smaller pool of orders available for subsequent delivery points to a July–September sales decline of at least 5%.

March total net revenue fell $185.3 million despite a $208.7 million increase in subscription and services revenue (A, B). Fewer bitcoin sales drove weakness even as a higher average bitcoin price cushioned it (D). I expect services growth to keep June above -5%, with a further decline in bitcoin volume putting July–September total revenue at risk of crossing -5%.

March revenue rose about 15% year over year to $105.5 million, yet lower demand caused inventories to increase $4.7 million during the quarter (A, B). The March growth gives June room to stay above -5%. The inventory buildup points to weaker shipments if demand stays soft into July–September, when I forecast the crossing.

March total revenue fell 3.4%. Dedicated freight revenue grew $9.5 million, partly offsetting declines in Expedited, Managed Freight, Warehousing and fuel surcharges (A, B). I expect Dedicated growth to keep June above -5%. With four sources of revenue already falling, a smaller Dedicated offset could widen the July–September decline to at least 5%.

UPS began reconfiguring its network in anticipation of lower volumes from its largest customer (E). The scale of that response points to a material shipment reduction. I forecast a gradual reduction that leaves June revenue above -5% year over year and takes July–September to -5% or worse. The filing gives no quarterly reduction schedule.
